Models & Pricing

Model prices are listed in units of per 1M tokens. A token, the smallest unit of text that the model recognizes, can be a word, a number, or even a punctuation mark. We bill model usage based on the total number of input and output tokens by the model.

(1) Use deepseek-flash as the model name. The legacy names deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp are still accepted, but the corresponding models have been retired, their requests are served by the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 model and billed at the Flash price.

(2) Off-peak rates are half of the peak rates. Peak hours are 01:00 - 04:00 and 06:00 - 10:00 UTC, Monday through Friday, excluding Chinese public holidays. All other hours are off-peak, including weekends and Chinese public holidays in full.

(3) For more details on concurrency limits, please refer to Rate Limit & Isolation.

Web Search & Fetch Pricing​

Search (text, image) and web fetch are billed per use, whether you call the Search and Fetch APIs directly or the model uses them through tools such as the web tools.

ItemUnitPrice
Search (text, image)Per 1,000 searches$0.75
Web fetchPer 1,000 fetches$0.75

For the billing rules, see Search & Fetch and Web Tools.

File Parsing & OCR Pricing​

ItemUnitPrice
File parsing, OCR APIPer 1,000 pages$0.225

Speech Pricing​

APIUnitList priceLimited-time price (50% off)
Text to Speech (TTS)Per 10,000 characters$0.45$0.225
Speech to Text (ASR)Per hour of audio$0.116$0.058

Deduction Rules​

For model usage, the expense = number of tokens × price. Search (text, image) and web fetch are charged per use at the rates above. The corresponding fees will be directly deducted from your topped-up balance or granted balance, with a preference for using the granted balance first when both balances are available.

Product prices may vary and DeepSeek reserves the right to adjust them. We recommend topping up based on your actual usage and regularly checking this page for the most recent pricing information.

模型调用费用 = token 消耗量 × 模型单价；搜索（文字、图片）和网页抓取按上表价格按次计费。对应的费用将直接从充值余额或赠送余额中进行扣减。 当充值余额与赠送余额同时存在时，优先扣减赠送余额。

产品价格可能发生变动，DeepSeek 保留修改价格的权利。请您依据实际用量按需充值，定期查看此页面以获知最新价格信息。

• Tool APIs
  • Search & Fetch
Open Markdown

Search & Fetch

The Search API and the Fetch API give agents and RAG applications access to live web content:

  • Search API finds web pages for a query and returns structured results. It is powered by DeepSeek's in-house search engine.
  • Fetch API retrieves a single web page and returns its content as Markdown.

Both are raw JSON APIs. They use the same bearer authentication as the DeepSeek API.

To have the model search and read pages by itself during a conversation, use the web tools instead.

The Search API does not support image search yet; support will be added later. For now, image search is available only through the web tools.

The base URL is https://api.deepseek.com:

APIEndpoint
SearchPOST https://api.deepseek.com/v1/tools/search
FetchPOST https://api.deepseek.com/v1/tools/fetch

See the Search API Reference and Fetch API Reference for the complete request and response schemas.

Authentication​

Send your API key and the JSON content type in the request headers:

HeaderRequiredValue
AuthorizationYesBearer <DeepSeek API Key>
Content-TypeYesapplication/json

Search API​

Request​

curl https://api.deepseek.com/v1/tools/search \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <DeepSeek API Key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "query": "DeepSeek V4 release",
    "count": 5,
    "need_content": true
  }'
import requests

response = requests.post(
    "https://api.deepseek.com/v1/tools/search",
    headers={
        "Authorization": "Bearer <DeepSeek API Key>",
    },
    json={
        "query": "DeepSeek V4 release",
        "count": 5,
        "need_content": True,
    },
)
response.raise_for_status()

for result in response.json()["results"]:
    print(result["title"], result["url"])
    print(result["summary"])

Request fields:

FieldTypeRequiredDefaultDescription
querystringYes-The search query must contain 1 to 128 Unicode characters, cannot be all whitespace, and supports the query operators listed below.
countintegerNo10The number of results to return, between 1 and 50.
ori_questionstringNo-The user's original question that triggered the search, between 1 and 128 characters, to improve query understanding, with null treated as not provided.
localizationstringNo""An optional IP address used to localize search results.
need_contentbooleanNofalseWhether to return page content in content, which is always an empty string when false.

Unknown fields in the request body are ignored.

Query Operators​

The query is forwarded with its search syntax intact. The examples below combine operators with a search term; you can combine multiple operators in one query.

OperatorExampleDescription
site:DeepSeek site:github.comRestrict results to the given site, and to target multiple sites, separate the site: clauses with spaces and join them with OR, for example DeepSeek site:github.com OR site:huggingface.co.
-site:DeepSeek -site:example.comExclude the given site, and separate multiple sites with spaces.
-DeepSeek -advertisementExclude pages containing the term, and separate multiple terms with spaces.
-"..."DeepSeek -"release notes"Exclude pages containing the exact phrase, which can contain spaces, and separate multiple phrases with spaces.
"..."DeepSeek "exact phrase"Match an exact phrase, and separate multiple phrases with spaces.
lang:DeepSeek lang:zh,enRestrict results to the given language codes, separating multiple codes with commas, for example lang:zh,en.
after:DeepSeek after:2025 or DeepSeek after:2025-01-01Restrict results to pages published after a date.
before:DeepSeek before:2026 or DeepSeek before:2026-06-01Restrict results to pages published before a date.

For example:

{
  "query": "DeepSeek site:github.com OR site:huggingface.co lang:en after:2025",
  "count": 10
}

Response​

A successful request returns HTTP 200 with a results array. A normal search with no matches returns an empty array.

{
  "results": [
    {
      "rerank_score": 2.4,
      "title": "DeepSeek V4 model released",
      "url": "https://example.com/deepseek-v4",
      "snippet": "DeepSeek V4 is now available, with tool calling and long-context support.",
      "summary": "DeepSeek has released the V4 model. The release adds improved tool calling and long-context support for agent workflows.",
      "content": "DeepSeek V4 is now generally available...",
      "site_name": "Example News",
      "site_icon": "https://example.com/favicon.ico",
      "date": "2026-06-01T00:00:00+00:00",
      "authority": 3
    }
  ]
}

Each item in results contains:

FieldTypeDescription
rerank_scorenumberA relevance score from 0 to 3 that combines signals such as relevance, authority, and freshness, with scores of 1.5 or above considered high-quality results.
titlestringThe title of the result.
urlstringThe URL of the result.
snippetstringA short summary related to the query, typically 100 to 200 characters, intended for display in a UI.
summarystringA long summary related to the query, typically 600 to 800 characters, intended to be read by a model.
contentstringThe page content, which is empty when need_content is false or when the content is unavailable.
site_namestring or nullThe name of the site, or null when unavailable.
site_iconstring or nullThe URL of the site icon, or null when unavailable.
datestring or nullThe publication time in UTC, formatted as RFC 3339, or null when unknown.
authorityintegerThe authority tier of the page, 0 to 4 (-1 means unknown), with values of 3 or above indicating highly authoritative sources.

Fetch API​

Request​

curl https://api.deepseek.com/v1/tools/fetch \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <DeepSeek API Key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "url": "https://example.com/article"
  }'
import requests

response = requests.post(
    "https://api.deepseek.com/v1/tools/fetch",
    headers={
        "Authorization": "Bearer <DeepSeek API Key>",
    },
    json={"url": "https://example.com/article"},
)
response.raise_for_status()

page = response.json()
print(page["title"])
print(page["content"])

Request fields:

FieldTypeRequiredDescription
urlstringYesThe page URL to fetch, which must be at most 8192 characters, an HTTP or HTTPS URL with a host, and must not contain a username or password.

Response​

{
  "title": "Example article",
  "content": "# Example article\n\nArticle content."
}
FieldTypeDescription
titlestringThe title of the page, empty when the title is unavailable.
contentstringThe fetched page content as Markdown text.

Fetching is subject to the target site's availability and access policies.

Errors​

Errors follow the OpenAI-compatible error format. The param field is always null.

{
  "error": {
    "message": "'count' must be between 1 and 50",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "param": null,
    "code": "invalid_request_error"
  }
}
HTTP StatusDescription
400The request headers or body are invalid, including malformed JSON or an invalid field value.
401The API key is missing or invalid.
402The account has insufficient balance.
403The Fetch request was rejected by the security policy.
404Fetch could not retrieve usable page content, for example due to an unavailable URL, a URL blocked by site policy, an error from the target site, an unsupported content type, or a page with no extractable Markdown content.
408Reading the request body timed out.
413The request body is too large.
429The Search or Fetch QPS limit was exceeded.
500An internal server error occurred.
504A downstream request timed out.

Search and Fetch are read-only. For HTTP 408, 429, or 5xx errors, wait and retry. For HTTP 402, top up your account before retrying. Do not retry other 4xx errors without changing the request.

Billing​

Search and Fetch are billed per successful request, not by tokens or by the number of returned results:

APIUnitPrice
SearchPer 1,000 successful requests$0.75
FetchPer 1,000 successful requests$0.75

A request is billable only when it returns HTTP 200 and produces a result (Search must return a non-empty results array, and Fetch must return page content). Failed requests, empty search results, and timeouts are not billed. count only controls how many results are returned and does not affect the per-request price.

Search and Fetch calls triggered by tools when using the DeepSeek API through DeepSeek Harness, Claude Code, or Codex, including Codex Alpha Search, are also billed per successful request.

The web tools are billed at the same web search and web fetch prices.

Rate Limits​

For each account, Search and Fetch are limited independently, and traffic to one does not consume the other's quota:

APIQPS Limit
Search100
Fetch25

The QPS (requests per second) limits are calculated at the account level, regardless of which API key is used, and are separate from the model concurrency limits. Requests above the account-level QPS limit receive HTTP 429. In addition to the account-level limit, Fetch is also subject to a per-domain QPS limit, and requests above that limit also receive HTTP 429.

Usage and Billing

The usage in the final message_delta, or in a non-streaming response, is the billed usage of the whole request, summed over its inference steps:

FieldMeaning
input_tokensInput tokens not served from the context cache
cache_read_input_tokensInput tokens served from the context cache
output_tokensOutput tokens
output_tokens_details.thinking_tokensThe thinking tokens among them, returned when thinking is enabled
cache_creation_input_tokensAlways 0
server_tool_use.web_search_requests, web_fetch_requestsThe numbers of search result blocks and fetch result blocks in the response, including errors. They are for display and are not billed counts
server_tool_use.tool_search, tool_fetch, tool_image_searchThe billed numbers of searches (excluding image searches), fetches and image searches

Tool calls are billed separately, at the web search, image search and web fetch prices in Models & Pricing, the same prices as the Search and Fetch APIs:

  • Web search: a search call that returns results is billed for each of its queries, so a call with three queries counts as three. A call that fails or returns no results is not billed.
  • Image search: each image counts as 1 search, and each region the model selects in an image counts as 1 more. A search that fails or finds no results is not billed.
  • Web fetch, URL reading: per page fetched successfully, including pages whose result is then replaced by a url_not_allowed or unavailable error under model content safety. Links that cannot be fetched are not billed.
  • Web fetch, deep thinking search: an opened page is billed only when it is fetched from the web. Opening the same page again, moving through a page, and opening a page whose content came with the search results are free.
  • Finding text in a page is free.

POST 
/anthropic/v1/messages
stream booleannullable

Default value: false

If true, return named server-sent events (SSE), ending with message_stop. There is no data: [DONE] message. Otherwise, return one complete message object.

usage

required

Possible values: >= 0

Input tokens not served from the context cache. Total input tokens equal input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens.

cache_creation_input_tokens integerrequired

Possible values: 0

Always 0. Anthropic-style cache creation is not used; context caching is automatic.

Possible values: >= 0

Generated output tokens, including thinking tokens when thinking is enabled. In message_delta this is the cumulative count, not an increment.

output_tokens_details

object

Breakdown of output_tokens. Present when thinking is enabled or safety_check is high.

thinking_tokens integer

Possible values: >= 0

Thinking tokens, already included in output_tokens.

Possible values: >= 0

DeepSeek extension. Tokens of the safety review, already included in output_tokens. Present only when safety_check is high.

Possible values: standard

server_tool_use

object

Server-side web search and fetch counts, separate from token usage. Present only when at least one of the counts is greater than zero; otherwise omitted. All fields are present when this object is returned. Read the final message's usage for non-streaming responses or the final message_delta.usage for streaming responses. These counts are cumulative, not deltas. See Server tool usage.

web_search_requests integerrequired

Possible values: >= 0

Number of server-side web search attempts, including failed attempts and attempts exceeding max_uses.

tool_search integerrequired

Possible values: >= 0

Number of successful server-side web searches that returned nonempty results. Failed attempts and empty results are not counted. This field can be used as a basis for billing.

web_fetch_requests integer

Possible values: >= 0

With the web tools. Number of fetch result blocks in the response, including errors. For display only.

tool_fetch integer

Possible values: >= 0

With the web tools. Number of billed page fetches.

tool_image_search integer

Possible values: >= 0

With the web tools. Number of billed image searches.

# File Parsing

## Billing


- **At upload**: billed once per page of the document, only when parsing succeeds, at the price in [Models & Pricing](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing.md#ocr-pricing).
- **In chat**: parsing is not billed again. Each chat request that references the document is billed for its input tokens at the model's input price.

# OCR ## Billing | Billing unit | Price | | --------------- | ------ | | Per 1,000 pages | $0.225 | Billed by the number of pages recognized successfully (`page_count`). A recognition that fails or times out is not billed. Disconnecting does not cancel a recognition: once the file has been received, the recognition runs to the end and is billed if it completes. ***

POST 
/v1/tools/ocr
page_count integerrequired

The number of pages, equal to the length of pages.

usage

object

required

The token usage of all pages. For reference only; not used for billing.

input_tokens integerrequired

The OCR input tokens of all pages. For reference only; not used for billing.

output_tokens integerrequired

The OCR output tokens of all pages. For reference only; not used for billing.

total_tokens integerrequired

The sum of input_tokens and output_tokens.

# Text to Speech ## Billing | Billing unit | List price | Limited-time price (50% off) | | --------------------- | ---------- | ---------------------------- | | Per 10,000 characters | $0.45 | $0.225 | A Chinese character counts as 2 characters; any other character, such as a letter, digit or space, counts as 1. ***

# Speech to Text ## Billing | Billing unit | List price | Limited-time price (50% off) | | ----------------- | ---------- | ---------------------------- | | Per hour of audio | $0.116 | $0.058 | Billed by audio duration to the second; a fraction of a second counts as 1 second. ***
